records.region: Argentine Puna, Salta–Catamarca: southern Pocitos o Quirón surroundings, northern Vega Juncalito, Salar de Antofalla and its eastern and southeastern marginal terrain.
records.material_pending_reason: The historical cartography does not establish the substantial selected northern passage into the Vega Juncalito feeder or the longitudinal eastern and southeastern Antofalla connections continuing to the actual selected terminal. The independent local wetland study supplies only limited prior prose, not the unavailable figure or a trunk-river connection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No whole selected natural-river identity established. Salar de Antofalla and the two mapped Vega Juncalito settings are bounded saline-basin/wetland context, not names for the complete modeled river.
records.completion_scope: Two successful historical IGN original views expose the selected regional terrain and distinguish nearby saline basins, wetlands and separately mapped rivers. They establish a northern local feeder to Vega Juncalito and Antofalla saline-basin context, but not the full opening connection from the Pocitos-side terrain, the longitudinal eastern salt-margin linkage or the long southern continuation and final westward turn. Those are actual ordinary through-link gaps, not an exact-bank requirement or merely absent whole-route naming.
records.supported_name_scope: No whole selected natural-river identity established. Salar de Antofalla and the two mapped Vega Juncalito settings are bounded saline-basin/wetland context, not names for the complete modeled river.

scope_limits: No uniformly named natural river or completed representative system identity is established for this modeled selection.
The northern Pocitos-side opening, eastern saline-margin continuity and long southern/terminal linkage remain material source gaps.
The salt-flat and wetland names remain useful bounded geographic components; adjacent Río Antofalla and Río Calalaste must not be imposed on the route.
No current continuous surface flow, exact seasonal water limit, current extraction operation, engineered connector or formal naming status is inferred.
The model length is not an official river length; absent generalized map linework is not proof that a natural drainage does not exist.

records.region: Southeast Greenland inland ice, toward the ice/rock margin at the inland side of Napasorsuup Kangerlua / Napasorsuaq Fjord.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established. Napasorsuup Kangerlua / Napasorsuaq Fjord is the mapped neighboring coastal-water setting, not a river-name candidate.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The regional original covers the chosen opening, all selected parts and joins, the lower ice/rock approach and the actual selected terminal. It establishes their terrain setting but supplies no representative natural-river name or evidence that the modeled sequence is one continuous surface or subglacial river.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected opening lies in inland ice. The line first travels northeast and turns south, then trends east and southeast through lower ice containing scattered exposed rock. Its final position belongs to the historical mapped ice/rock margin beside the fjord-head setting. Neighboring glacier, coast and fjord labels are not extended over the modeled river group.
records.completion_scope: All 64 stored parts and their joins were examined against contiguous regional original cartography, including the opening, northern arch, southeastward continuation, lower-margin bends and final selected position. The regional map’s northern and eastern neatlines do not cut the selected route. National cartography provides supporting broad inland-ice/coastal context. There is no substantial unviewed geographic interval at ordinary source scale.

component_scope_limits: The fjord name identifies coastal water and provides terminal-setting context only. It is not assigned to the selected inland-ice sequence.
Glacier/ice-path terrain correspondence is not evidence of a natural river or a surface/subglacial hydraulic link.
The national legend distinguishes surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments; these are not a surveyed river network.
No selected lake, reservoir or managed-channel connector is established by the inspected originals.
The historical maps do not verify present-day glacier-front positions, exact terminal bank placement or current drainage behavior.
A null candidate means the inspected sources did not establish the name; it does not claim that no local or official name exists.

bounded_name_observations.role: Neighboring fjord-head coastal-water context only; no river candidate or exact modern ice/land/water endpoint assigned.

records.region: Southern Ecuador; northeastern Nabón headwaters, León valley, Jubones corridor and selected coastal ending near Machala.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported representative receiving-system candidate, with incomplete correspondence of the selected lower coastal route.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected final coastal-plain passage and actual ending are southwest of the downstream Jubones course and more northerly Canal de Jambelí outlet shown in the inspected CELEC map and MCRJ basin map reproduced in the thesis. Their broad basin setting does not establish that selected through-link. It is not a question of choosing an exact bank, mouth vertex or formal name-change point.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Río León names the selected upper natural component. Río Jubones identifies the receiving middle and lower river. Neither name is extended over the unestablished final coastal passage, and Jubones is not asserted as a uniform scalar name for the León component or the reservoir.
records.completion_scope: The selected northeastern opening, León descent and northward hook, receiving Jubones junction and westward middle course, Minas San Francisco reservoir/dam setting, and lower valley east of the coastal divergence have bounded correspondence. The final lower-plain route and terminal remain materially unestablished. No completed representative-system identity or completed name-scope hold is claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: Río León names the selected upper natural component. Río Jubones identifies the receiving middle and lower river. Neither name is extended over the unestablished final coastal passage, and Jubones is not asserted as a uniform scalar name for the León component or the reservoir.

scope_limits: The actual selected coastal-plain through-link and terminal have not been matched; no alternative name or natural-water connection is invented.
Representative Jubones evidence does not extend one scalar name to the separately named León component or to managed water.
Hydronym-boundary vertices, current reservoir operations and exact coastal shorelines are outside this bounded investigation.
Historical map dates and secondary source credits are retained; no present-day full-system verification or formal registry lookup is claimed.

records.region: Eastern James Bay, Québec; unnamed eastern feeder, Lac du Vieux Comptoir, Rivière du Vieux Comptoir and its James Bay outlet.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the connected receiving-river system. The eastern headward feeder is not named in the inspected originals; the selected lake retains its separate lake identity. The river name is not assigned as a scalar label to every selected part.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded historical cartographic correspondence for the chosen eastern opening, every selected part, the inlet and through-lake passage, the southwestern lake outlet, intervening river junctions, the lower coastal branching setting and the actual James Bay terminal. The source linework establishes these connections at ordinary corridor scale; neither nearby labels nor reserve/basin membership is used to replace a missing link.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected receiving-river system. The eastern headward feeder is not named in the inspected originals; the selected lake retains its separate lake identity. The river name is not assigned as a scalar label to every selected part.

scope_limits: The eastern feeder remains unnamed in the two inspected originals; this does not erase its observed connection to the receiving named system.
Formal registry status, exact naming boundaries, official source and mouth positions, and a Korean name are unverified.
The selected modeled length is not an official named-river length.
The originals are historical regional cartography. Current channel condition, lake level, hydraulic operation, navigability and tidal shore position are outside this finding.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
